title: SDK Launchpad: First 3 Days checklist & playflows
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, actionable launchpad to get a new developer from zero to a small production-ready integration within three days using Redwood SDKs. It is intentionally pragmatic: minimal steps to validate the happy path, then safe expansion into CI, telemetry, and rollout controls.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: backend engineers and platform integrators who need to add text generation, chat, or embedding calls to an existing service.
- Scope: SDK install, basic usage patterns, local-mode smoke tests, CI wiring, telemetry contracts, and a production readiness checklist. Not a full API reference.

Acceptance criteria (end of day 3):
- Developer can install SDK, call a model, and stream a response locally.
- Integration is covered by a CI smoke test that runs in PRs.
- Basic telemetry (latency, token counts, error rates) emits to our observability pipeline.
- A canary rollout config exists in the repo and a runbook for common failures is documented.

Day 0 - pre-reqs (to be completed before Day 1):
- Create Redwood account and API key with developer scope. Tag key with repo name.
- Clone sample-app template: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-samples/starter-proxy.
- Ensure local docker and docker-compose installed, node or python runtime available.
- Add an issue to RDW-1234 for any infra requests (VPC, secrets).

Day 1 - happy path quickstart (goal: working request locally)
1) Install SDK
   - npm: npm install @redwood/inference or pip: pip install redwood-sdk (pick language binding).
2) Configure credentials
   - Add REDWOOD_API_KEY to local env, or write a minimal .env file.
3) Run the sample server
   - Start local proxy: docker-compose up -d dev-proxy (this mirrors network behavior for Private).
4) Make a call
   - Run the sample script: examples/generate_simple.{js,py}
   - Confirm 200 and a plausible text response.
5) Verify streaming and function calling
   - Use the streaming sample to ensure chunked payloads arrive.
6) Quick sanity checks
   - Token accounting: check SDK returns token usage metrics in response metadata.
   - Error modes: simulate an invalid key to confirm proper 401 handling.

Day 1 deliverables:
- PR created against starter-proxy with env setup and README instructions.
- Local runbook snippet committed: README section titled "Quickstart - first 30 minutes."

Day 2 - shaping reliability and developer ergonomics (goal: CI + local-mode fidelity)
1) Add CI smoke test
   - Test should run one short generation and assert response length > 10 and status 200.
   - Use a small model or sandbox mode to avoid cost. Add test to CI pipeline with token injection via CI secrets.
2) Local-mode fidelity
   - Provide docker-compose profile that mimics production routing: local proxy + a stubbed model backend returning canned responses.
   - Add a health-check endpoint that uses the SDK to call the real service; in local-mode point it to stub.
3) Telemetry contract
   - Standardize fields: request_id, sdk_version, model_name, token_input, token_output, latency_ms, error_code.
   - Emit logs at INFO for success, WARN for retries, ERROR for permanent failures.
   - Add a short example of structured logging for Node and Python.
4) Tracing and correlation
   - Ensure SDK picks up incoming trace headers (x-trace-id) and forwards them. Add an example using OpenTelemetry stub.

Day 2 deliverables:
- CI test passing in PR for starter-proxy.
- Example docker-compose for local-mode added to repo.
- Short telemetry README and sample logging snippet committed.

Day 3 - production readiness and rollout playflows (goal: safe rollout and alerting)
1) Canary and gradual rollout
   - Add a feature flag or route-level config: start at 5% traffic, monitor for 24 hours, then 25, then 100. Use the Redwood Console route override where possible.
2) Alerts and SLOs
   - Create alerts for: 95th percentile latency > 1.5x baseline, error rate > 1% over 10m, token usage spike > 3x expected.
   - Define on-call play: page SRE if sustained error rate > 2% for 15m.
3) Fallbacks and graceful degradation
   - Implement fallback policy: if primary model fails or latency > threshold, switch to cheaper smaller model and annotate response.
   - Add user-facing messaging templates for degraded mode.
4) Release and docs
   - Finalize README with known limitations, cost expectations, and recommended model profiles for low-latency vs high-quality.
   - Add a changelog entry and a version bump in SDK manifest.

Day 3 deliverables:
- Canary config in repo and short monitoring dashboard link.
- Runbook section with triage steps for common failure modes.
- Release PR with version bump and changelog.

Runbook snippets (to copy into repo docs)
- If 401 returned: rotate key, confirm env, verify secrets manager path. Ticket template: OS-SECRET-ROTATE.
- If latency spike: check 95th percentile across models, verify autoscaler and GPU pool metric, fallback to smaller model, open ticket SRE-LATENCY.
- If increased hallucinations or quality regression: revert to pinned model version, run eval suite against golden prompts, open RDW-QUAL-<repo>.

Telemetry example (pseudo):
- log line: {level: INFO, request_id: <id>, model: gpt-xx, tok_in: 42, tok_out: 125, latency_ms: 210, sdk_ver: 0.8.1}
- Trace header: x-redwood-trace: <trace-id> - include in outbound request metadata.

CI considerations
- Use token-scoped sandbox keys for CI to avoid billing surprises.
- If running full integration tests, gate them behind a nightly pipeline.
- Mock network failures in unit tests to ensure retry logic behaves as expected.

Integrations and examples to include in repo
- Minimal Express/Flask route demonstrating streaming to browser.
- Embeddings sample with small local SQLite index for semantic search.
- Sidecar pattern example for long-running services.

Known open questions and risks
- Rate limit behavior for bursty traffic patterns - need an integration test under realistic load (ticket: RDW-3456).
- Telemetry schema alignment across languages - propose canonical JSON schema and add linters.
- Docs clarity for Private deployments - need a separate short doc for network/topology.

Next steps and owners
- Diego - add CI smoke test and sandbox key rotation docs (owner for RDW-1234).
- Lena - create telemetry JSON schema and add linters.
- Samir - implement docker-compose local-mode and stubbed endpoints.
- Aisha - consolidate this doc into the starter-proxy README and open the release PR.

Appendix - quick command cheatsheet
- Install: npm i @redwood/inference or pip install redwood-sdk
- Run local proxy: docker-compose -f docker-compose.local.yml up --build
- Run simple generator: node examples/generate_simple.js or python examples/generate_simple.py
- Run CI smoke: ./ci/run-smoke.sh

Notes and rationale:
- Keep Day 1 extremely frictionless to get a psychological win. Day 2 focuses on reliability hygiene. Day 3 is about safety and observability. This three-day rhythm has worked well as a template for internal platform integrations.

End of document.
